list.name: runner
list.label: Runner (regex)
list.description: Filters the deadchannel Runners, Recent Beats, and Haunt Log panels by username regex. Empty matches everyone.

panels.title: Throughput (RPS)
panels.description: HTTP requests only: server spans, without the readiness probe (/api/health answers 503 on purpose while an old pod drains) and the long-lived sockets and streams (/api/ws/pair, /api/listen, /listen/state), whose span lasts as long as the connection.

panels.title: Error Rate (%)

targets.expr: sum by (service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", http_route!~"/api/health|/api/ws/pair|/api/listen|/listen/state", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / (sum by (service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", http_route!~"/api/health|/api/ws/pair|/api/listen|/listen/state"}[5m])) > 0) * 100

panels.description: HTTP requests only: server spans, without the readiness probe (/api/health answers 503 on purpose while an old pod drains) and the long-lived sockets and streams (/api/ws/pair, /api/listen, /listen/state), whose span lasts as long as the connection.

panels.title: p99 Latency (ms)
panels.description: HTTP requests only: server spans, without the readiness probe (/api/health answers 503 on purpose while an old pod drains) and the long-lived sockets and streams (/api/ws/pair, /api/listen, /listen/state), whose span lasts as long as the connection.

panels.title: Slowest Operations (p95)
panels.description: p95 duration of every traced operation (HTTP routes, service tasks, outbound calls) over the range, operations with at least 20 calls. Session-long loops are left out: their span lasts as long as a session. A parent and its child span both appear (a task and the work it wraps).

targets.expr: topk(15, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, service_name, span_name) (increase(traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service", span_name!~"chat.refresh_registration|chat.poll_finalizer|cyberspace.circ_stream|cyberspace.circ_presence|.*key=.*"}[$__range]))) and on (service_name, span_name) (sum by (service_name, span_name) (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"$service", span_name!~"chat.refresh_registration|chat.poll_finalizer|cyberspace.circ_stream|cyberspace.circ_presence|.*key=.*"}[$__range])) >= 20))

panels.title: Time Spent by Operation
panels.description: Total time inside each operation over the range (calls x average). Where the server's time goes, as opposed to what is slow: a fast operation called constantly ranks high here. Same exclusions as the p95 panel; nested spans count in both parent and child.

panels.title: Session Start by Stage
panels.description: Time from TCP accept to the first frame on screen, over the range. auth: SSH handshake and user lookup. bootstrap: key accepted to the App built (every preload). first_frame: App built to the first drawn frame. total: all of it, what a user waits in front of a blank terminal.

panels.title: DB Pool
panels.description: Pooled Postgres connections in use against the pool ceiling (worst pod per service), callers queued for a connection, and chat read permits held (of 8). In use at the ceiling with waiters above zero means the pool is the bottleneck; permits at 8 means chat reads queue on their own semaphore first.

panels.title: DB Checkout Wait
panels.description: Time Db::get waits for a pooled connection (p95, p99), and failed checkouts per second (the 5s pool timeout, or a backend that would not connect). Rising wait with a flat query time is pool pressure, not slow SQL.

panels.title: Notify Re-reads
panels.description: Every notify-driven re-read of shared state (pg_listener::read_until_ok), by domain: p95 of one attempt, and failed attempts per second. A domain failing here is a replica serving stale state (or, right after a reconnect, none) and retrying every 5s until the read lands.

panels.title: Top INFO Messages
panels.description: Most frequent INFO messages - spot noisy logs worth silencing.

targets.expr: {service.name=~"$service"} severity:INFO | stats by ("service.name", _msg) count() info_logs_total | sort by (info_logs_total desc) | limit 8

panels.title: Top WARN Messages
panels.description: Most frequent WARN messages - early warning signal before things escalate.

targets.expr: {service.name=~"$service"} severity:WARN | stats by ("service.name", _msg) count() warn_logs_total | sort by (warn_logs_total desc) | limit 8

panels.title: Top Error Messages
panels.description: Highest-count raw ERROR messages in the selected time range. Useful for seeing repeated noise before filtering it.

targets.expr: {service.name=~"$service"} severity:ERROR | stats by ("service.name", _msg) count() error_logs_total | sort by (error_logs_total desc) | limit 8

panels.title: Log Volume by Severity
panels.description: Log count stacked by severity - red ERROR bursts are visible at a glance.

panels.title: Service Logs
panels.description: Selected service logs for first-pass investigation.

panels.title: Error Logs: late-web
panels.description: Severity ERROR logs for late-web.

panels.title: Error Logs: late-ssh
panels.description: Severity ERROR logs for late-ssh.

panels.title: Recent Traces: late-web
panels.description: Latest late-web traces from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: Recent Traces: late-ssh
panels.description: Latest late-ssh traces from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: Recent Error Traces: late-web
panels.description: Recent late-web traces with error spans from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: Recent Error Traces: late-ssh
panels.description: Recent late-ssh traces with error spans from VictoriaTraces.

panels.title: SSH Sessions
panels.description: Current active SSH sessions

panels.title: SSH Traffic
panels.description: SSH connections and successful client pairings

panels.title: Interaction Rate
panels.description: Chat sends, votes, and page views

panels.title: Reliability Signals
panels.description: Frame drops and late-web now-playing fetch results

panels.title: CLI Pair Starts
panels.description: Pair session starts by SSH mode and client platform

panels.title: CLI Pair Active
panels.description: Current active pair sessions by SSH mode and client platform

panels.title: Daily Puzzle Wins by Mode
panels.description: Boards solved on a session over the range, daily and personal apart. Counted where the board ends, so personal boards (never a GameWon) show here too.

panels.title: Daily Puzzle Wins by Difficulty
panels.description: Solved boards by difficulty, both modes. Le Word and Rubik's Cube have one board a day and are left out.

panels.title: Share Rate per Daily Win (%)
panels.description: Share cards copied per fresh daily win. The number that says which daily people brag about.

panels.title: Win Rate, Losable Dailies (%)

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (game, mode, difficulty) (increase(late_ssh_arcade_finishes_total{finish="won",game=~"le_word|minesweeper"}[$__range])) / sum by (game, mode, difficulty) (increase(late_ssh_arcade_finishes_total{game=~"le_word|minesweeper"}[$__range]))

panels.description: Won over finished boards for the two dailies that can be lost (Le Word out of guesses, Minesweeper out of lives).

panels.title: Active Time by Screen
panels.description: Session time on each screen with a key pressed in the last five minutes. Idle terminals left open are counted apart (presence=idle).

panels.title: Active Time by Game
panels.description: Active session time with a game open, by game: Arcade boards (dailies and score runs) and House Table games (poker, blackjack, asterion, tron, ssnake). Door games are screens of their own, in Active Time by Screen.

panels.title: Sessions per Screen (active)
panels.description: Seconds of active attention per second: the average number of active sessions looking at each screen.

panels.title: Door, Table & Match Wins
panels.description: Wins outside the Arcade dailies. Lateania is left out: its GameWon fires per mob kill (family=lateania), which would drown the rest.

panels.title: Visits by Place
panels.description: Arrivals on each screen (and place inside it: Home room kind, Arcade board or House Table game, Profiles shelf, Artboard canvas or gallery) over the range, top 15. Sampled on the 1Hz edge, so a place passed through in under a second is not a visit.

panels.title: Active Time per Visit

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (screen, place) (increase(late_ssh_attention_seconds_total{presence="active"}[$__range])) / (sum by (screen, place) (increase(late_ssh_place_visits_total[$__range])) >= 5))

panels.description: Active seconds over arrivals, per screen and place, for places with at least 5 visits in the range. How long a stop lasts once someone is there.

panels.title: Jobs & Artboard Split
panels.description: Active time on the two shelves of Profiles (people, jobs) and the two halves of the Artboard (canvas, gallery). The Jobs number is the reach the nightly press pays for.

panels.title: Home by Room
panels.description: Active time on Home by what the chat pane shows: #lounge (the Home card), a kind of room (language, public or private topic, DM, deadchannel), or a rail entry (feeds, news, cyberspace, notifications, discover, showcase, work).

panels.title: Home Visits by Room
panels.description: Arrivals on each Home room kind or rail entry over the range. Switching between two rooms of the same kind is no new arrival.

panels.title: Zork Launches
panels.description: Play sessions started over the range, by edition and what they loaded: auto (the autosave; Continue on the game already open resumes it and counts nothing), manual (the manual save), new (a fresh story). A switch from a live game counts once the old one has checkpointed.

panels.title: Zork Session Ends
panels.description: How play sessions ended over the range. quit: the player quit the story. returned: RESTORE, or a switch, checkpointed back to the menus. idle: closed after 20 minutes without game input. busy: the account's game was held by another session, or the host was shutting down. save_rejected: the chosen save was invalid or unavailable. crashed: any other exit, or the channel closed without one. connect_failed: connect, auth, the launch request, or the stream broke.

panels.title: Zork Switches, Save Reads & Suggestions
panels.description: switch: leaving a live game for another edition, a manual load, or a new game. switched means the old game checkpointed and the next one started; save_failed means it closed without a checkpoint exit; timed_out means no exit within 8s, so the old game stays open. saves: the menus' read of the account's six slots; a failure shows 'Unable to read saves'. suggestion: F3 on a player's own game, typing a watcher's '>' command (typed), refused off an empty prompt (not_at_prompt), or with none waiting (none_waiting).

panels.title: Zork Trouble
panels.description: What should stay at zero: sessions that ended crashed, connect_failed, busy, or save_rejected; switches that did not switch; failed save-slot reads. A wall of connect_failed is the late-zork host down or its secret out of step with late-ssh.

panels.title: Render Rate
panels.description: Frames drawn (by trigger) vs clean world ticks that skipped the draw entirely (the dirty gate)

panels.title: Clean Skip Ratio (%)
panels.description: Share of render passes the dirty gate skipped; higher = more idle sessions settling clean

panels.title: Draws per Session
panels.description: Average frames drawn per second per active session (pre-adaptive baseline was ~15; mostly-idle fleet should sit well under 2)

panels.title: Render Stalls
panels.description: Output-budget guard: paused render passes and forced disconnects for clients not reading their stream. Input budget hits: passes that stopped handing a session's queued input to the app at 64 messages or 4 ms (a key flood or a slow handler) and left the rest for the next pass.

panels.title: Terminal Round Trip
panels.description: Server writing a status query (DSR) to the user's terminal answering it: network both ways, any backlog ahead of the query, the ssh client, the terminal's parse. Split by the bytes the session wrote in the second before the query, the pass that carried it included (none, small up to 4 KiB, medium up to 32 KiB, large). Large well above none means bytes on the wire are what users feel as lag.

panels.title: Round Trip by Client
panels.description: Terminal round trip over the range, by client (plain ssh or the late CLI) and the bytes written in the second before the query.

panels.title: Frame Size
panels.description: Bytes of each drawn frame handed to the SSH channel, by render reason. A frame is a ratatui diff; terminal commands (images, OSC) are not in it.

panels.title: Session Output Rate
panels.description: One session's SSH output (frames plus terminal commands) averaged over 10 s windows, across sessions. p95 is the heavy sessions: animated screens, the screensaver, images.

panels.title: Probe Answer Rate (%)
panels.description: Share of round-trip probes the terminal answered within 30 s. A session whose terminal ignores three in a row stops probing, so a low rate is a terminal without DSR support or a link stalled for 30 s.

panels.title: CLI Trip Split
panels.description: For native-mode late CLI sessions, the whole trip the server timed next to the two halves the CLI timed: ssh_rtt is the SSH transport alone, terminal is the user's terminal alone (query out of the CLI to its answer back).

panels.title: Render Pass Time
panels.description: How long one render pass held the app lock (input drain, tick, draw), across sessions. The red line is the hot tick (66 ms): a p99 above it for minutes is a session pinning a tokio worker while the fleet's CPU average stays green. `_msg:"slow render pass"` in VictoriaLogs names the user and screen.

panels.title: Render Pass p99 by Screen
panels.description: p99 render pass time per screen the pass ended on. One screen far above the rest is where to look.

panels.title: Output Bytes by Place
panels.description: Bytes sent to users over the range, by the screen and place the session was on and whether anyone was at the keys (idle: no key in five minutes, so nobody is watching). Frames and terminal commands (images, OSC) together, top 15. Where the bandwidth goes: a popular screen ranks high even when each viewer is cheap.

panels.title: Output Bytes per Active Second
panels.description: Bytes sent per second of active attention, per screen and place with at least a minute of it in the range, top 15. What one watching viewer costs on that place, whatever its popularity: the animations worth slimming rank here.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (screen, place) (increase(late_ssh_output_bytes_total{presence="active"}[$__range])) / (sum by (screen, place) (increase(late_ssh_attention_seconds_total{presence="active"}[$__range])) >= 60))

panels.title: Presence Wire
panels.description: Batches this replica sent (published) and heard from other replicas (heard), per second. Published runs at most 5/s (one per 200ms flush with changes) plus a heartbeat every 3s, whatever the headcount; heard is the other replicas' published. See app/presence.

panels.title: Presence Trouble
panels.description: What should stay at zero. expired: another replica's sessions dropped after 10s without a heartbeat (a replica died, or a LISTEN dropped and a leave was missed). publish_failed: the database refused a notify (the next heartbeat resends). rejected: a payload that did not parse (a replica on another wire format mid-deploy).

panels.title: Sessions in Presence
panels.description: Who every replica thinks is here. local is each replica's own sessions, summed; seen is every record a replica holds, shown for the replica seeing the most and the fewest. The two seen lines should sit on top of each other: a gap that lasts past a heartbeat means a replica is missing someone. SSH sessions for scale.

panels.title: Nightcap Orders
panels.description: Pours off the Nightcap menu over the range: poured (chips moved), comped (a round credit paid), bounced (the tab would not cover it), failed (the chip write did not land). Rounds count in the next panel, whichever bar sold them.

panels.title: Rounds & Gift Drinks
panels.description: Drinks bought for other people over the range, at either bar: rounds bought and the drinks they granted and that were cashed, gift drinks, and why the house refused the rest.

panels.title: Nightcap House Failures
panels.description: The bar's off-thread work that failed over the range: credit_count (the menu's free-drink count) and house_line (the house saying a pour out loud). What a healthy order counter cannot see: a stale menu or a quiet bar.

panels.title: Bartender Memory
panels.description: Every write to @bartender's memory of a patron over the range, by outcome: exchange_stored and requested_stored (kept), turned_away (said before a "forget me"), already_stored, wiped (a "forget me" landed), and the three *_failed, which never show in the room: an exchange is stored off the reply path, and a failed remember or wipe gets no line.

panels.title: First Contact Ladder
panels.description: Beats delivered per stage over the selected range. Counters are per-pod and reset on restart, so this sums each pod's high-water mark instead of the live value: a deploy never zeroes the ladder.

panels.title: Gate Verdicts
panels.description: Connects by eligibility verdict, the same reset-safe sum. One count per connect, not per person: which leg turns people away, and how often.

panels.title: Bio Screens
panels.description: AI bio-screen outcomes. Claimed once per bio text per day, so a flapping API costs at most one call per person per day.

panels.title: Beats Over Time
panels.description: When the ladder actually fires. Bars are beats per interval by stage; the slow burn should show as scattered singles, never a cluster.

panels.title: Runners
panels.description: One row per person on the ladder, read off the deadchannel log lines: the highest glitch, name, and whisper hit seen, when the invitation went out and when they joined, how many sessions armed, when they were last seen, and the latest gate verdict with its three legs (hours need 8, settings keys need 2, bio needs 100 chars before a screen is spent). Logs keep 7 days, so a rung reached earlier than that shows as an empty cell: users.settings stays the source of truth. Filter with the Runner variable or the column filters.

targets.expr: _msg:"first contact" OR _msg:"deadchannel joined" | filter username:* | filter username:~"$runner" | stats by (username) max(hits) if (_msg:"clock glitch burst") glitch, max(hits) if (_msg:"name flicker hit") name, max(hits) if (_msg:"whisper delivered") whisper, max(_time) if (_msg:"invitation sent") invited_at, max(_time) if (_msg:"deadchannel joined") joined_at, count() if (_msg:"first contact armed") sessions, max(_time) last_seen, row_max(_time, verdict, active_hours, touched_settings, bio_chars, bio) if (_msg:"gate evaluated") last_gate | unpack_json from last_gate fields (verdict, active_hours, touched_settings, bio_chars, bio) | delete last_gate | sort by (last_seen desc)

panels.title: Recent Beats
panels.description: What just happened on the ladder, newest first: hits (forced ones say so), whispers, invitations, joins, runner births, bio screens, and /haunt flag flips. Arming and gate lines are left out; they live in the Runners table and the Haunt Log.

targets.expr: _msg:"clock glitch burst" OR _msg:"name flicker hit" OR _msg:"whisper delivered" OR _msg:"invitation sent" OR _msg:"deadchannel joined" OR _msg:"runner created" OR _msg:"first contact bio screen" OR _msg:"haunt flag set" | filter username:* | filter username:~"$runner" | fields _time, _msg, username, hits, outcome, key, enabled | sort by (_time desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Haunt Log
panels.description: Every deadchannel line in one place, newest first: the gate, arming, each hit, the whisper, the invitation, the admin switches, and the runner's birth. The username is formatted into the message itself because the logs panel renders _msg and nothing else; expand a row for the counters and the trace id. The Runner variable filters it like the tables above.

targets.expr: _msg:"first contact" OR _msg:"haunt flag" OR _msg:"runner created" OR _msg:"deadchannel joined" | filter username:~"$runner" | format "[<username>] <_msg>" as _msg

panels.title: Fights by Beat
panels.description: The fight at the screen over the range, by what happened (exchanges inside a fight, beat=round, are left out so the outcomes stay readable): started or resumed, won, slain, lost, escaped, and the armorer's outfitted and patch's patched, with refused and failed.

panels.title: Tailor, Prints & the Door
panels.description: Looks worn at the tailor's mirror (worn, no_runner, failed), posters saved and burned at PRINTS (saved, burned, no_runner, failed; the read on open: read_failed, undecodable), and runners leaving and returning to #deadchannel over the range.

panels.title: Old Signal Payouts
panels.description: Old Signal kills over the range by what the chips did: paid, refused by the 30-day lockout (inside_month), or the grant failing.

panels.title: Lounge Spawns
panels.description: The lounge spawns (deadchannel/lounge) over the range: spawned, hit, slain, slipped; hitters paid, left (no standing runner), or failed; hits refused or failed.

panels.title: Day-One Active Minutes by Screen
panels.description: Minutes with a key press behind them, from accounts in their first 24 hours, by screen, over the selected range.

panels.title: Tour Stops Reached
panels.description: First-visit tour stops reached over the selected range, from the welcome box at the door on. Each stop is one Enter past the one before, so the drop between two bars is where newcomers leave the route. A newcomer who leaves mid-tour starts over at the welcome box next session, a new attempt; /onboard reruns are not counted.

panels.title: Where Day-One Sessions End
panels.description: The screen that was up when a first-day account's session ended, over the selected range: the last thing a newcomer saw.

panels.title: Sessions by Tenure
panels.description: Sessions started per day from accounts on their first day, in their first week, and older. First-week sessions against first-day ones is the cheapest view of whether newcomers come back; the per-person funnel is the AUDIENCE.md query.

panels.title: Daily Posts and Deliveries
panels.description: The herald's one post a day (late-ssh app/herald) over the range: posted, skipped (nothing worth posting), lost (another replica had the day), failed (retried up to three times, then the day rests); and each network's leg of it, delivered or failed. One 'posted' or 'skipped' a day is the healthy line; a 'failed' with no 'posted' after it is a day missed, and the network rows say which leg.
